name: Screen-Space Ray Casting with Adaptive Step Size
definition: A pixel shader technique that renders volumetric scattering by casting rays from the camera through each pixel into a 3D texture, accumulating in-scattered radiance using an adaptive step size based on density changes and transmittance.
summary: Screen-Space Ray Casting with Adaptive Step Size is a pixel shader technique that renders volumetric scattering by dynamically adjusting sampling intervals based on density changes to maintain fidelity while skipping empty space.
